pr.title: feat(rules): multi-condition mute rules with per-field regex
pr.body:
feat(rules): multi-condition mute rules with per-field regex

<!-- git-stk:description -->
Lets one `[[rules.mute]]` rule combine conditions — all must match (AND) — so you can scope a mute instead of muting a whole author:

```toml
[[rules.mute]]
author  = "github-actions[bot]"
excerpt = "CircleCI pipeline triggered"
```

Flat fields (`author`/`title`/`excerpt`, each with an optional `<field>_regex`) compose with the existing single `match`/`pattern` form (unchanged, still works). A rule with **no** conditions is a config error — otherwise "all match" is vacuously true and it would mute the whole feed.

Closes #54.
<!-- /git-stk:description -->

<!-- git-stk:closes -->
Closes #54
<!-- /git-stk:closes -->

expected.description: The excerpt condition is compiled with title_regex instead of excerpt_regex, so `excerpt_regex = true` is ignored (the pattern is matched as a substring) and setting title_regex turns the excerpt pattern into a regex.
